paragraphs: The Z4 sDrive23i and sDrive28i were part of the E89 generation, produced from 2009 to 2016. Both use engines from BMW's N52 family — a naturally aspirated straight-six petrol engine that was one of BMW's last non-turbocharged six-cylinder designs. The sDrive23i uses the 2.5-litre version, while the sDrive28i uses the 3.0-litre unit, offering a useful power increase. The N52 is known as a generally reliable engine family, with none of the major structural issues seen on some other BMW petrol sixes — though like any engine of its age, regular maintenance is key to long-term reliability.
about.boldParagraph: The Z4 sDrive23i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.5-litre naturally aspirated straight-six petrol, fitted to the sDrive23i from 2009 to 2016. Part of BMW's N52 engine family — generally reliable with no major structural flags. We replace timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.
cards.cta: Check Your N52 BMW Z4 sDrive23i

cards.body: A 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six petrol, fitted to the sDrive28i from 2009 to 2016. The same N52 family as the 2.5-litre unit, but with greater displacement and power. Known as a generally reliable engine with no major defect pattern confirmed. We service it to the same standard as the 2.5-litre unit, replacing timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as needed.

compatibility.intro: The E89 Z4's N52 family spans two displacements — 2.5-litre and 3.0-litre — which are closely related but not interchangeable. Fitting the wrong displacement engine to your car would mean ECU mismatches and a car that doesn't run correctly. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

Any ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Z4 quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
